Event:  The Philippines will host the Association of Southeast Asian Nations’ (ASEAN) 49th Summit and related summits in Metro Manila on November 16–18, 2026. The main venue is the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC) in Pasay City. The Government of the Philippines declared November 16–18 special non-working days in the National Capital Region. Expect heavy security, road closures, and traffic disruptions across Metro Manila before and during the summit. Announced measures include:  Road closures in Pasay : Partial closures around PICC and the CCP Complex starting October 24. Full closures from November 9 to November 20. Expect severe congestion on Roxas Blvd., Diokno Blvd., Macapagal Blvd., Buendia Ave., and the World Trade Center area. Some bus lanes will become restricted “ASEAN lanes” for official convoys. Restrictions on public events : Fun runs, motorcades, processions, and other outdoor gatherings near the summit venues are suspended from October 24 to November 20. Flight cancellations : Philippine Airlines and Cebu Pacific have cancelled or rescheduled many domestic and international flights to and from Manila from November 14 to 18. Demonstrations : Some groups have announced protests during the summit. Actions to Take:  Check your flight status directly with your airline. Leave extra time to get to NAIA and expect longer security screening. Avoid the PICC/CCP area and Roxas Boulevard from November 9 to November 20. Plan for sudden road closures and convoy stops anywhere in Metro Manila. Avoid demonstrations. Even peaceful gatherings can turn confrontational. Stay alert in areas where crowds gather. Follow instructions from Philippine authorities and carry ID if you live or work inside restricted zones. Monitor local media and official advisories from the Metro Manila Development Authority (MMDA) and local government units. The U.S. Embassy in Manila remains open for routine and emergency services but the public is advised to monitor our website for announcement on changes to Consular Section hours or appointments for November 16–18. ———————————————————- For further information and assistance: Enroll in the  Smart Traveler Enrollment Program  (STEP) to receive Alerts and make it easier to locate you in an emergency. Contact the U.S. Embassy in Manila, Philippines, located at 1201 Roxas Boulevard, at +(63) (2) 5301-2000, from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. After-hours emergency number for U.S. citizens is +(63) (2) 5301-2000. Call 1-888-407-4747 toll-free in the United States and Canada or 1-202-501-4444 from other countries from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time, Monday through Friday (except U.S. federal holidays). See the State Department’s  travel website  for the Worldwide Caution, Travel Advisories, Alerts, and the  Philippines Country Specific Information . Follow us on  X  and  Facebook .
